picks.headline: University of Delaware joins Google Books Library Project to curate scholarly sources for AI training
picks.excerpt: The University of Delaware Library announced it has joined the Google Books Library Project, committing to digitize more than 100,000 volumes within three years and preserve them in HathiTrust. Vice Provost Trevor A. Dawes said contributing vetted, well-curated academic volumes with retained source attribution will help ensure future AI systems are trained on reliable, scholarly sources rather than scraped pirate libraries.
picks.rationale: Net-new, distinct URL and content from every published books card. Reframes the library/AI-training debate around consented, curated scholarly corpora with source attribution — a concrete institutional move rather than another lawsuit story.

picks.headline: Hong Kong Book Fair centers its 2026 edition on 'Reading for All in the Age of AI'
picks.excerpt: The 36th HKTDC Hong Kong Book Fair closed July 21 under the theme 'Reading for All in the Age of AI: Reshaping and Co-evolution.' At the International Publishing Forum and IP Roundtable, which drew more than 250 participants, publishers explored how AI could raise reading efficiency and cultivate critical, in-depth thinking, and how cross-sector cooperation could foster reading culture.
picks.rationale: Net-new AI angle distinct from the already-carded IPA Congress AI panel; a snapshot of how a major Asian trade fair frames AI's role in reading and publishing. Second books pick takes a distinct palette accent (#7928ca) and motif from the first.
